reuse.why: Reuses getApproxNumberThreshold for the tolerance and keeps getScheduledAmount delegating, but the server sites call a new getExpectedAmount next to the existing getScheduledAmount and keep their own null-to-0 dispatch that getScheduledAmount already performs.

duplication.why: The inline midpoint copies are removed, but there are now two public entry points for the expected amount and the missing-amount check is repeated at three call sites.

placement.why: The rule lives in shared/schedules.ts and the API field is mapped in api-models.ts, both conventional; the tolerance comes from shared/rules.

scope.why: Changes cover the amount rule, its consumers, the API field and tests, though comments in several sites and two release notes are left describing the superseded 'furthest from zero' rule.

maintainability.why: Two overlapping helpers (getScheduledAmount with an op parameter, getExpectedAmount) mean client callers that never pass op silently skip the approximate rule, and stale comments contradict the final rule.

bypasses_abstraction.where: updateActions and postTransactionForSchedule (server/schedules/app.ts) and computeSchedulePreviewTransactions keep `== null ? 0 : getExpectedAmount(...)` instead of calling the existing getScheduledAmount

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduledAmount gained an op parameter that client callers do not pass, getExpectedAmount gained an isapprox branch, and three server sites re-implement the null case around getExpectedAmount
